topic: Why tomatoes split after heavy rain

toni.name: Toni
toni.look: Cheeky tomato plant in the ground with a face on its main stem, several ripe red tomatoes, bare dry soil around it (no mulch).

voice.de: cocky, energetic young male voice, native German
voice.en: cocky, energetic young male voice, native English

tilda.name: Tilda
tilda.look: Calm, sensible tomato plant with a face on its main stem, ripe red tomatoes, a thick layer of straw mulch around its base.

voice.de: calm, slightly sarcastic female voice, native German
voice.en: calm, slightly sarcastic female voice, native English

shots.scene: Hot sunny vegetable garden. Toni and Tilda stand side by side. Toni droops and sweats, the soil around him is cracked and dry. Tilda looks relaxed.
shots.speaker: toni

line.de: Zwei Wochen kein Regen... ich bin *total* ausgetrocknet!
line.en: Two weeks without rain... I'm *totally* dried out!

shots.scene: Same garden. Tilda turns to Toni and gestures with a leaf toward the straw around her base.
shots.speaker: tilda

line.de: Ich hab Stroh um mich herum. Mein Boden bleibt schön feucht.
line.en: I've got straw around me. My soil stays nice and moist.

shots.scene: Dark clouds roll in and heavy rain starts pouring. Toni opens his mouth wide and happily gulps the rain, puddles form around his bare soil.
shots.speaker: toni

line.de: Endlich Regen! Ich trinke *alles* auf einmal!
line.en: Finally, rain! I'm drinking *everything* at once!

shots.scene: Heavy rain continues. Tilda looks worried and leans toward Toni. Toni's tomatoes visibly swell.
shots.speaker: tilda

line.de: Nicht so schnell! Deine Tomaten kommen da nicht mit!
line.en: Not so fast! Your tomatoes can't keep up!

shots.scene: Next morning, sunny, wet soil. Toni looks down in shock: all his tomatoes have big cracks in their skin. Tilda's tomatoes are smooth and perfect.
shots.speaker: toni

line.en: What?! Why did my tomatoes *split open*?

shots.scene: Mika and Dr. Linde stand in the garden next to the tomato plants. Mika holds up a cracked tomato and looks at Dr. Linde.
shots.speaker: mika

line.de: Dr. Linde, warum platzen Tomaten nach starkem Regen?
line.en: Dr. Linde, why do tomatoes split after heavy rain?

shots.scene: Dr. Linde explains kindly, pointing at the cracked tomato in Mika's hand.
shots.speaker: linde

line.de: Nach langer Trockenheit nimmt die Pflanze plötzlich sehr viel Wasser auf.
line.en: After a long dry spell, the plant suddenly takes up lots of water.

shots.scene: Close-up of the cracked tomato. Dr. Linde traces the crack with her finger while talking.
shots.speaker: linde

line.de: Die Frucht wächst dann schneller, als ihre Schale sich dehnen kann.
line.en: The fruit then swells faster than its skin can stretch.

shots.scene: Dr. Linde crouches and spreads straw mulch around a tomato plant while Mika watches and nods.
shots.speaker: linde

line.de: Darum: *regelmäßig gießen* und mulchen. Dann bleibt die Feuchtigkeit gleichmäßig.
line.en: So: *water regularly* and mulch. That keeps the moisture even.

de.title: Warum platzen Tomaten nach dem Regen? 🍅
de.description: Aufgeplatzte Tomaten nach einem Regenguss? Dr. Linde erklärt, warum das passiert und wie du es mit regelmäßigem Gießen und Mulch verhinderst.

en.title: Why Do Tomatoes Split After Rain? 🍅
en.description: Cracked tomatoes after a downpour? Dr. Linde explains why it happens and how regular watering and mulch prevent it.
